newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS details asset management operations.
newsitem.headline: UBS details asset management operations.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said that although its asset management company in the U.S. has been successful in both money market and bond products, its equity business was unsatisfactory.
"Our asset management company in New York has not yet found its definitive position in the U.S. market," UBS chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said.

However, he said institutional asset management business in Singapore got off to "very promising" start, and several years of intensive efforts in Japan have paid off with several major clients being acquired, he said.
In addition, UBS Asset Management London, Ltd, with assets under management of around 120 billion Swiss francs, once again achieved an excellent result.
But in terms of investment performance, it lagged behind the competition in 1996.

He said the main causes for this were a strict implementation of the value investment style, which resulted in disappointing results across the globe in 1996, and its over-cautious valuation of the U.S. market.

In a further review of operations, he said underwriting and corporate finance business had an increase of earnings of roughly 50 percent and this area contributed almost half a billion Swiss francs to fee and commission income.

UBS said its private equity business performed particularly well in the year under review, and that its equity primary business performed well both in selected industries such as technology, telecommunications and life sciences, as well as in emerging markets.
